instruction: Extract the helloExtension.zip file from /home/user/Desktop/ to the same directory and load it as an unpacked extension in Chrome.

parameters.command: echo {CLIENT_PASSWORD} | sudo -S apt-get update -y && echo {CLIENT_PASSWORD} | sudo -S apt-get install unzip -y && unzip /home/user/Desktop/helloExtension.zip -d /home/user/Desktop/ && rm /home/user/Desktop/helloExtension.zip

metadata.explanation: Variation emphasizing 'enable' action. Task requires unpacking the extension zip and enabling it in Chrome. Evaluator leverages existing Chrome functions: get_find_unpacked_extension_path extracts all extension paths from Chrome's preference file, is_in_list metric confirms the expected extension path is present in the loaded extensions list.
metadata.verification: Verified evaluator logic: Extension paths stored in Chrome preferences JSON under extensions.settings, getter function parses all paths, metric performs string-in-list check.

llm_judge_reasons: Evaluator correctly verifies both unpacking and enabling requirements: getter reads Chrome's extensions.settings which only contains actively loaded/enabled extensions, not just any unpacked folder
Logic flow is semantically correct: getter extracts all extension paths from Chrome Preferences JSON → metric checks if expected path '/home/user/Desktop/helloExtension' is in the result list
Expected value is semantically accurate: matches the unpacked directory path created by the setup command 'unzip /home/user/Desktop/helloExtension.zip -d /home/user/Desktop/'
No runtime issues: Chrome Preferences file is persistent and readable after task completion, no UI state dependency, no postconfig needed
Complete coverage: implicitly verifies unpacking (path must exist) and explicitly verifies enabling (path must be in Chrome's loaded extensions settings)
